Subject: On-prem / air-gapped deployment — next steps & hardware Qs

Hi Chris —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Recap and agreed next steps from our side:

- LegacyBank is leaning toward a Private on-prem (air-gapped) deployment for PROD due to regulatory/data residency controls.
- Shortlist of immediate info we need to continue pricing and SOW:
  - Target production capacity (qps / concurrent sessions) and model family you expect to run (LlamaX-70B / mix of smaller models?)
  - Preferred GPU types you have on-prem (A100/H100 availability) or if you want Redwood to specify hardware.
  - Offline upgrade/patching constraints: can you accept maintenance windows for offline bundle installs via USB/airgap transfer, or must upgrades be zero-downtime?
  - KMS/HSM requirements for key material and whether customer-managed KMS is mandatory.

Attachments: redwood-onprem-checklist.pdf (high-level items we usually need).

Short answer on a few we discussed: Redwood supports both A100 and H100 backends; we can provide quantized variants to reduce GPU memory. Offline upgrades are supported via signed upgrade bundles delivered to your airgap admin — the process requires a brief maintenance window (typically 10–30 minutes per service node) unless you run a multi-node rolling upgrade schedule. Dev will follow up with the exact upgrade playbook.

Can you share the network diagram and security contact so we can line up a technical workshop?

Goal: get the infra checklist and security POC this week and schedule a 60-min workshop (security + infra + SE).

Thanks —

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Capacity: initial pilot ~50 concurrent sessions, target steady-state 500 concurrent sessions within 6 months. Models: we want to run a mix — primary production will be a 70B-class model for document summarization and a 13B for embedding / reranking.
- Hardware: Our data center currently has racks with NVIDIA A100 40GB and a small H100 pool we can provision for critical workloads. We can also procure additional H100s if needed.
- Offline upgrades: Security requires that any inbound software to the air-gapped environment be delivered via signed media and validated by our infra team. Short maintenance windows are OK as long as they're scheduled and we get rollback instructions.
- KMS: We must use our HSM for key material; integration details can be shared with your SE.

Hi Aisha / Chris —

Thanks for the diagram and the details. Quick technical notes and what we will bring to the workshop:

1) Supported hardware
- Redwood runtime supports A100 (40GB, 80GB) and H100. For a 70B-class model we recommend H100 or A100 80GB with multi-node sharding to meet latency SLOs.

2) Capacity sizing (ballpark)
- Pilot (50 concurrent): 2–4 x H100 nodes or 4–6 x A100-80GB nodes depending on latency targets.
- Steady-state (500 concurrent): cluster sizing depends on batching policy; expect ~12–20 H100 nodes or 20–40 A100-80GB nodes. We'll finalize this in workshops using your request profile.

3) Offline upgrade process
- We provide signed upgrade bundles (SHA256 + PKI cert) that your infra team transfers into the air-gapped environment. An offline verification step checks signature and checksums before install.
- Typical maintenance window: 10–30 minutes per node for software replace + service restart. For multi-node clusters we support rolling upgrades to keep service available; if your security requires a full freeze, we can run a batch upgrade with a longer scheduled window.
- Rollback: upgrade bundles include a guaranteed rollback snapshot and procedure; we test rollback in our staging prior to delivery.

4) KMS/HSM integration
- We support customer-managed KMS/HSM via PKCS#11 or an appliance-based key wrapping flow. We'll prepare a short integration spec for your HSM vendor.

5) Troubleshooting / offline logs
- We can ship a diagnostics bundle that runs locally and produces a signed artifact your team can review without internet access.

Attachment: redwood-offline-upgrade-playbook.txt (outline of the bundle & steps).

Next steps:
- Proposed times for 60-min technical workshop (PST): Thu 2026-07-23 10:00 or Fri 2026-07-24 14:00. Please confirm Aisha / Chris.
- We'll bring an SE, an infra engineer and a short sizing worksheet.
